**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Stalk section showing an intact (not shredded) tan/light brown rind
- Numerous tiny black dots densely scattered across the entire stalk surface
- Node visible at left edge
- No shredding of pith visible — stalk structure still intact

**Reasoning:**
- The test image shows the stalk exterior with hundreds of tiny black fruiting structures on a light tan/brown internode
- **Charcoal stalk rot**: Reference shows shredded pith with gray vascular strands — does NOT match (the test stalk is intact)
- **Diplodia stalk rot**: Described as "numerous small black dots (pycnidia), about the size of a pinhead or smaller, on the lower internodes" on what appears to be a bleached/tan stalk — this matches the intact stalk with dense tiny black pycnidia
- **Anthracnose stalk rot**: Would show shiny black streaks/blotches on the rind, not uniform tiny dots

The dense distribution of pinhead-sized black pycnidia on an intact, light tan stalk exterior is the hallmark of Diplodia stalk rot.
